meeting_header:
Date: 2025-03-04 | Start: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 52m
Attendees: Sam Torres (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Alex Wu (Redwood Solutions); John Keller (NimbusPay Head of ML), Maya Singh (NimbusPay Security), Ravi Patel (NimbusPay Eng Manager)
summary: POC scoping focused on data handling for pilot: PII redaction, logging/retention settings, prompt storage concerns. Discussed success criteria (latency, throughput, quality), workload sizing for benchmarks, Dedicated vs Private options, encryption/KMS, and an initial 2-4 week pilot timeline.
transcript:
00:00 Sam (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining, quick intros?
00:07 John (Customer): John here, head of ML at NimbusPay. Maya and Ravi are with me.
00:12 Priya (Redwood SE): Hey all, Priya from Redwood, I'll run the POC setup and benchmarks.
00:18 Speaker 1: Sound good.
00:25 Maya (Security): We mostly want to understand how you handle PII in prompts — like card numbers, names, emails — and what you store.
00:32 Sam: Totally. So, high level, Redwood can run hosted, we have Dedicated reserved pools, and Private VPC/on-prem. For POC you usually see two tracks: hosted with strict retention or Dedicated/Private where you can control storage.
00:45 Ravi: For us, default is we don't want prompts persisted in logs, or at least redacted. What's the redaction story?
00:52 Priya: Right, so we have a few knobs. We can enable prompt redaction at ingest, configurable patterns, and we support suppressing transcript logs — it's, uhm, not on by default for hosted API, but for Dedicated/Private you can disable or route logs off. We also support prefix/KV cache — note cache can store keys, we can configure to not persist KV cache to long term storage.
01:12 Maya: Are redaction rules regex-based? Can we supply custom patterns?
01:16 Priya: Yes, you can supply custom regex patterns and we can apply a two-step pipeline: client-side pre-redaction (recommended) plus server-side redaction. There's also a mode where prompts are hashed rather than stored in plain text.
01:29 John: Hashing ok, but we need reproducibility for evals — if we hash, can we still run exact-match retrievals?
01:36 Priya: Hashing preserves deterministic mapping if you manage the keys; but if you need semantic search over prompts, we recommend generating embeddings and storing them with redacted text. We also offer ephemeral embeddings that are not persisted beyond the retention window.
01:50 Speaker 2: mhm
01:55 Sam: On retention: hosted default is 30 days for logs and 90 days for some telemetry; for POC we can set retention to 7/30/90 depending on your compliance needs. For Dedicated/Private you get tenant-level control and can set retention to zero — meaning logs are not stored — or short-term only.
02:12 Maya: Do you support customer-managed KMS?
02:15 Priya: Yes, for Dedicated and Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault). For hosted we have server-side encryption at rest but can also offer bring-your-own-key in enterprise plans.
02:27 Ravi: Good. On the benchmark side, our target success criteria: p50 latency under 150ms for short chat flows, throughput to sustain ~5 QPS steady with spikes to 20 QPS, and quality: less than 3% regression vs our current baseline for key NLU tasks. Cost target ideally under $X per 1M tokens but that's negotiable.
02:48 Priya: Helpful. Can you share sample workload shape? avg prompt length?
02:52 John: Typical prompt 150-250 tokens, model completions ~100-200 tokens. Peak concurrent users ~20, sustained 5 qps. Average monthly tokens estimate ~25M tokens for pilot workload.
03:07 Priya: Ok, so rough sizing: with 5 QPS and avg 350 tokens per request (prompt + completion) that's ~1.75k tokens/s, or about 6.3M tokens an hour if sustained — for a short benchmark run we'll do smaller windows. We'll propose Dedicated instance type that gives you predictable throughput; or Private if you require VPC isolation.
03:28 Maya: Our security requirement: audit logs for admin actions, RBAC for who can see prompts, SSO via SAML, and exportable audit trail.
03:36 Sam: Redwood Console provides per-token tracing, role-based dashboards, and audit logs. For privacy-sensitive setups we can mask prompt contents in the console UI and surface only redaction markers.
03:46 Speaker 1: right
03:50 Maya: About logging — can you disable debug-level logs that might capture full prompts?
03:54 Priya: Yes. We can run with production log level and ensure debug is off. For POC we'll confirm the logging config.
04:01 John: How about function/tool calling — if we call internal connectors that echo PII, is that captured?
04:08 Priya: Those tool outputs are treated like responses; we can apply the same redaction pipeline and decide whether tool call payloads are stored. For extra safety, we recommend client-side redaction for sensitive fields before sending.
04:20 Ravi: Any concerns about KV cache leakage between requests?
04:24 Priya: KV cache is per-tenant/ per-session and in Dedicated we can keep it in memory only; for persistent caches we can configure TTLs and avoid writing to disk. We also have automatic prefix caching that can be disabled.
04:36 Speaker 2: ok
04:40 Priya: Now benchmarks: we'll run a 3-step benchmark: (1) functional correctness on a held-out eval set (quality/regression), (2) latency/throughput microbench with synthetic traffic to measure p50/p95 and tokens/s, (3) end-to-end scenario with real-ish prompts (anonymized) to capture tail behavior.
04:58 John: Timeline? We were hoping to have POC results in 2-4 weeks.
05:02 Priya: That works. Week 0: alignment + security docs and sample data; Week 1: infra setup (Dedicated node or Private env) and baseline benchmarks; Week 2: run full workload tests and quality evals; Week 3-4: iterate on configs, report and recommendations. So 2-4 weeks realistic.
05:20 Maya: For the POC, can you sign an addendum to restrict log retention and not store prompts?
05:25 Sam: We can do a POC addendum that sets data handling terms for the pilot — retention, redaction, and KMS requirements. I'll draft and share.
05:33 Ravi: Do you store prompts for model improvement?
05:36 Priya: No, Redwood does not use customer prompt data for model training unless explicitly opted in — enterprise agreements can forbid that. For hosted, default is we use telemetry for product improvement but we offer opt-outs and enterprise-level data isolation.
05:49 John: Good. Can we get a sample config for redaction rules and the retention settings?
05:53 Priya: Yes, we'll share a starter config (regex examples, retention options: 7/30/90/never) and a README on how to apply it in the POC.
06:02 Speaker 1: There was a question about storage of prompts in analytics — are they stored downstream in observability tools?
06:08 Sam: Observability tools ingest aggregates; raw prompts are not forwarded unless configured. We'll map the telemetry pipeline as part of the security pack.
06:16 Maya: What about PCI implications for card numbers in prompts?
06:20 Priya: For PCI, we recommend preventing any card numbers from ever being sent — client-side redaction should scrub PANs. If you must process them, you need a Private/on-prem deployment and specific contracts; we can discuss legal/PCI scoping separately.
06:35 John: For success criteria recap: latency p50 <150ms, p95 <400ms, throughput sustain 5 QPS with 20 spike, quality regression <3%, and data-handling controls in place.
06:46 Sam: Yep. And deliverables from our side: SOC2/ISO docs, POC addendum template, starter redaction config, benchmark harness and results sheet.
06:56 Maya: We'll provide anonymized prompt samples and PII patterns.
07:00 Priya: Ok, any other blockers?
07:03 Ravi: Need estimate of cost for Dedicated nodes for pilot.
07:07 Sam: We'll include cost estimates in the follow-up email.
07:10 Speaker 2: cool
07:12 Sam: Alright, recap of next steps: Sam to send security doc pack and addendum; Priya to provision benchmark harness; Maya to send PII examples; Ravi to prep VPC if Private path chosen. We'll sync early next week.
07:28 John: Thanks everyone.
07:31 End of call.

Notes: Transcript includes some ASR mistakes, occasional speaker mislabels. Shared artifacts referenced: security-pack.pdf (shared), benchmark-sheet.xlsx (link provided in follow-up).
